claims.claim: Origen of Alexandria was a Christian theologian born around AD 185 in Alexandria and died around AD 254 in Tyre.
He served as head of the Catechetical School of Alexandria, succeeding Clement, and later taught and was ordained a priest in Caesarea.
The work was written to present a spiritual (allegorical) interpretation of the Genesis creation narratives, seeking “a meaning worthy of God.”

The original Greek text of the Homilies on Genesis has been lost; what survives is a Latin translation made by Rufinus of Aquileia together with scattered Greek fragments preserved in the manuscript tradition.
The homilies survive today in a modern English translation published by the Catholic University of America Press, based on Rufinus’s Latin version.
Origen is regarded as the first Christian scholar to turn biblical exegesis into a systematic science, and his Genesis homilies have shaped later patristic interpretation and medieval mysticism.
